summary: Agent-memory frameworks increasingly expose distinct short-term and long-term stores; some also use the semantic, episodic, and procedural taxonomy directly.

items.text: LangGraph documents thread-scoped short-term memory and namespace-scoped long-term memory, then separates long-term content into semantic facts, episodic experiences, and procedural instructions. Its stores and checkpointers let applications assign different persistence and retrieval paths to each tier.

Letta uses always-visible memory blocks as constrained in-context memory while retaining conversation state and allowing external archival retrieval. Block labels, descriptions, size limits, and sharing make working-memory allocation explicit.

Zep separates a compact context block from a temporal knowledge graph and message history. It resolves changing facts in the graph before packaging selected context for an agent, implementing a distinction between durable memory and current working context.

Mem0 exposes scoped memories for users, agents, and runs together with filters, metadata, history, and semantic search. Applications can use those scopes as tiers, although semantic, episodic, and procedural classification remains an application responsibility.
